body.statement: Conditional on the radius delivered by \(\mathrm{oeq{:}arbitrary\mbox{-}density\mbox{-}frontier}\), derive a necessary-and-sufficient spectral criterion for \(T_n^{\mathrm{MMD}}\) and for some \(T_{n,\lambda_n}^{\mathrm{Wald}}\) to attain \(\delta_n^\star\) at each covariance exponent \(r\) and source exponent \(s\). The criterion must be an explicit eigenwise extremal ratio incorporating source-constrained signal, null effective dimension, higher-order nuisance remainder, and empirical-operator error; failure in either named statistic must be witnessed by a legal sequence in \(\mathcal M_1\).
body.justification: A method comparison is meaningful only after the all-tests modulus and nuisance amplification are in the same sequence experiment.
body.gap: Hagrass et al. classify direct two-sample filters under a different loss, while Jain and Luedtke analyze fixed regularization without an iff minimax criterion.
body.consumer: The criterion tells the 401(k) analyst when covariance whitening improves local power, when it only changes constants, and when it loses to identity weighting.

obligation.what_is_open: A necessary-and-sufficient eigenwise criterion for identity weighting and shrinking-resolvent weighting at the all-tests frontier.
obligation.obstruction: The all-tests frontier is unresolved, and the spectral handle gives no formula for the coordinatewise higher-order remainder or empirical covariance-operator error. Those quantities are indispensable to both sufficiency and a legal failing extremal sequence.
obligation.attempted: Population identity and resolvent quadratic forms were compared by spectral calculus. This proves equivalence for regularization bounded away from zero but supplies no conclusion for shrinking regularization.
obligation.partial_result:
Only a deterministic fixed-regularization comparison follows. For every \(\lambda\ge\lambda_0>0\) and \(\psi\in\mathcal H\), positivity and the spectral theorem give
\[
\frac{\|\psi\|_{\mathcal H}^2}{\|\Sigma_P\|+\lambda}
\le\langle\psi,(\Sigma_P+\lambda I)^{-1}\psi\rangle_{\mathcal H}
\le\frac{\|\psi\|_{\mathcal H}^2}{\lambda}.
\]
Thus a population resolvent bounded away from singularity is norm-equivalent to identity weighting and cannot change a separation exponent. No criterion for shrinking \(\lambda\) follows because the frozen handle supplies no eigenwise higher-order remainder or empirical-operator error.
